overview.description: Page One is a traditional Japanese shedding game where players must follow suit or draw until they can. It features a unique trick-taking loop where the objective is not to win tricks, but to empty your hand. The Joker acts as an invincible trump, and players must declare 'Page One!' when down to their final card to avoid heavy penalties.

history.origins: Developed in Japan during the 1950s and 1960s, separate from the 'American' Crazy Eights variant.
timeline: 1950s: Game first appears in Japanese social circles.
1970s: 'American' Crazy Eights variant begins to share the same name.
Present: Remains a popular introductory card game in Japan.
history.evolution: The game evolved from trick-taking roots into a shedding format with a draw-until-playable penalty system.
history.cultural: The name 'Page One' refers to reaching the final page (the last card) of one's hand.

setup.players: Two to six players sit in a circle; play proceeds clockwise.
setup.deck: Standard 52-card pack plus one Joker. Rank: Joker > A > K > Q > J > 10 > 9 > 8 > 7 > 6 > 5 > 4 > 3 > 2.
setup.equipment: One standard deck of 52 cards, one Joker, and a surface for the trick pile.
setup.dealing: Dealer gives four cards to each player, one at a time. Remainder is the stock.

rules.objective: Be the first player to play all cards from your hand to the trick pile.
rules.gameplay: 1. Lead: Player to dealer's left leads any card. 2. Follow: Players must follow suit if possible. 3. Draw: If unable to follow suit, draw from stock one-by-one until a playable card is found. 4. Joker: Can be played anytime to win the trick. If led, the next player sets the suit. 5. Next: Trick winner leads the next trick. 6. Page One!: Must declare 'Page One!' when down to one card or draw 5 cards.
keyRules: If unable to follow suit, must draw until a card of the led suit or Joker is found.
Joker always wins the trick; if led, the next card determines the suit for the following players.
Must declare 'Page One!' when playing second-to-last card or winning a trick with it.
Emptying the hand immediately wins the game.

strategy.basic: Save the Joker for a guaranteed win to take the lead. Use the lead to play suits your opponents might not have, forcing them to draw cards.
strategy.intermediate: Watch which suits are being drawn from the stock to identify which players are weak in specific suits.
strategy.advanced: Timing the Page One declaration is critical; bait opponents into drawing cards before you go out.
tips: Don't play high cards early unless you need to win the lead.
Remember that the Joker led sets a trap for the next player to determine the suit.
Always be ready to call 'Page One!' immediately upon playing your second-to-last card.

difficulty.easy: Plays cards randomly and often forgets the Page One declaration.
difficulty.medium: Understands suit following and uses the Joker logically to win tricks.
difficulty.hard: Tracks suits drawn by opponents and optimizes the Joker for the final play.

considerations: Must prioritize following suit to avoid drawing from the stock.
Strategic use of Joker to regain the lead.
Page One declaration monitoring for self and opponents.

ante.reason: Japanese Page One is a shedding game played without an ante or betting mechanism.

deal.reason: The initial dealing of cards is handled automatically by the game engine.

reveal_market.reason: This game does not utilize a market zone or market mechanics for card acquisition.

buy_market.reason: There is no currency system or market for purchasing cards in Japanese Page One.

buy_stock.reason: Cards are drawn from the stock as a penalty rather than being purchased by players.

fold.reason: Players cannot fold; they must continue playing until their hand is completely empty.

check.reason: This game does not include betting rounds or the option to check during play.

call.reason: Standard betting calls do not exist in this follow-suit shedding game.

bet.reason: Betting is not a component of the traditional Japanese Page One ruleset.

raise.reason: There is no betting mechanism, thus raising the stakes is not a valid action.

declare.reason: Melding declarations are not part of the game; see the Page One declaration action.

reveal_hand.reason: Player hands remain private until the cards are legally played to the trick pile.

award_pot.reason: There is no pot of chips or money to award in this card game.

play_card.description: Play a card from your hand into the current trick pile.
play_card.constraints: Must follow the led suit if possible; the Joker may be played anytime.

draw.reason: Drawing is handled via the draw_until_playable custom action during specific conditions.

discard.reason: Cards are played to tricks rather than being discarded into a shared pile.

pass.reason: Passing is not allowed; players must play a card or draw until they can.

bid.reason: Japanese Page One does not include a bidding phase to determine a declarer.

meld.reason: There are no melding mechanics or point-scoring card combinations in this game.

go_out.description: Play the final card from your hand to win the game deal.
go_out.constraints: Must have only one card remaining and have correctly declared Page One.
go_out.reason: This is the terminal winning action when a player successfully sheds all their cards.

drawSources.notes: Must draw until a playable card is found.

trickConfig.leadRestrictions: Winner of previous trick leads any card.

wildcards.restrictions: Always wins the trick; if led, next player determines the trick suit.

validPlays.notes: Must follow suit or play the Joker.

shedding.burnRules: Completed tricks are shuffled into stock when exhausted.

edgeCases.text: If Joker is led, the second player may play any card and that card sets the suit for the trick.
Failing to say 'Page One!' results in a 5-card penalty draw from the stock.

customActions.description: Dealer distributes four cards to each player, one at a time; the engine performs this automatically.
customActions.constraints: Dealer only; executed once at game start.
customActions.reason: Used by the deal phase to satisfy phase action requirement; actual deal is engine-handled.

customActions.description: Draw cards from the stock one-by-one until you obtain a card of the led suit or the Joker.
customActions.constraints: Can only be used if the player has no cards of the led suit in their hand.
customActions.reason: This is the core penalty mechanic when a player cannot follow the required suit.

customActions.description: Verbally declare 'Page One!' to notify opponents that you have reached your final card.
customActions.constraints: Must be performed immediately when playing your second-to-last card or winning a trick with it.
customActions.reason: This is a mandatory social declaration required by the rules to avoid card penalties.

engine.handRankingSystem: Shedding game; no hand ranking applies beyond individual card values.
engine.rankingSystem: High-card trick-taking within the led suit.
engine.deckDescription: Standard fifty-two card pack with one Joker added, totaling fifty-three cards used for play and stock.
engine.suitDescription: The four standard French suits: Hearts, Diamonds, Clubs, and Spades are used for follow-suit trick mechanics.
engine.rankDescription: Cards rank Joker (high), Ace, King, Queen, Jack, Ten, Nine, Eight, Seven, Six, Five, Four, Three, Two (low).
engine.dealPattern: Each player is dealt four cards one at a time in clockwise order from the dealer.

notApplicableReasons.discardConfig: Cards are played into a trick pile and removed rather than being discarded into a waste pile.
notApplicableReasons.buyCosts: There is no economy or currency system for purchasing cards in Japanese Page One.
notApplicableReasons.marketConfig: The game utilizes a single face-down stock pile rather than an open market of cards.
notApplicableReasons.fishingConfig: This is a follow-suit shedding game and does not use capture or fishing mechanics.
notApplicableReasons.patienceConfig: Japanese Page One is a competitive multiplayer game and is not designed for solitaire play.
notApplicableReasons.bankingConfig: There is no house banker or central banking mechanic involved in the gameplay of Page One.
notApplicableReasons.meldConfig: Players shed individual cards to tricks and do not form or lay down melded combinations.

hero.title: Page One
hero.subtitle: Japanese Shedding
hero.tagline: Follow suit, survive the draw, and declare your way to victory.

synthesis.shortDescription: A Japanese shedding game where you must follow suit or draw until you can. Call 'Page One!' on your last card or take a five-card penalty.

prompts.human: How do I play Page One?
prompts.ai: Page One is a Japanese shedding game. Follow the led suit if you can; if not, draw until you get a playable card. Don't forget to say 'Page One!' when you're down to your last card, or you'll have to draw five penalty cards.

scoring.description: None; first player to shed all cards wins the round.
scoring.winCondition: Shed all cards from your hand before any other player.

penalties.missing_declaration: Five card penalty draw from the stock.

assumptions: Follows Pagat's description of Japanese Page One mechanics.
